doc.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004

title: Producing the band himself and the Wooten brothers' Arista experience
summary: Fleck has always produced the Flecktones. Victor and Future Man distrusted outside producers after a bad experience with Kashif at Arista.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Have you found that you relate pretty well to outside producers?
We never had an outside producer. I produced the band from the very beginning.
That’s good. I think that’s a luxury.

Yeah I mean we’ve had pressure on us to have outside producers and early on I think Future Man was the one who didn’t want to have any part of it. Because he had had some bad experiences, Victor and Future Man, the Wooten brothers. There’s five of them. And they had a big deal at a certain point on Arista records and a fellow named Kashif who

produced I guess Whitney Houston and some other people and was producing them. And some bad things happened. Like they came in one day and Vic’s parts had been replaced by another bass player or a keyboard, or things like that. And they felt very taken advantage of and they were very suspicious of producers. And so for Future Man, who is doing something very unusual, he didn’t like the idea of some other person having a say about what he did. He was very un-into it at that point. And if it was the wrong producer that could have happened. But I was actually okay with it. I thought it would be neat to get like Daniel Lanois or somebody to help us paint a whole different sonic picture and go about things differently. But I’ve gotten really good at the technical part of taking the Flecktones into the studio and making it into a performance, you know, editing, doing things to capture the live moments and make a good take. We work really well as a team to do it and really we don’t need somebody else in there. Although there’s times it’s good to bring something different to the music. I would try it I guess.
